conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: INSPECT statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: identifier-3/4/5 overlapping identifier-1 -> result undefined (cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 'the result of the execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry' -> OK, same wording as 13)/18)/21)). The runtime matches against the ORIGINAL image and writes a separate buffer, every operand image is read before the store, so an overlap gives a deterministic result and no crash. No requirement to test. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: If identifier-3, identifier-4, or identifier-5 occupies the same storage area as identifier-1, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry. (See 14.6.10, Overlapping operands.)

rows.subject: INSPECT statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: identifier-4/6/7 overlapping identifier-1 -> result undefined (same wording as 13)/18), cite.py OK). from/to/delimiter images are read before Convert runs and the conversion reads a snapshot, so the outcome is deterministic and nothing crashes. No requirement to test. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: If identifier-4, identifier-6, or identifier-7 occupies the same storage area as identifier-1, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry. (See 14.6.10, Overlapping operands.)

rows.subject: INSPECT statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "the first occurrence of the character is used for replacement" -> OK GR23. Convert maps via fromSet.IndexOf(ch) — the first occurrence wins. Probe misc.cob: V='abcabc' CONVERTING "aab" TO "XYZ" -> XZcXZc (a->X by first occurrence, b->Z). InspectDifferentialTests.Convert_DuplicateFromCharacter_FirstOccurrenceWins is AssertSameAsLegacy (legacy differential) and does not close the row. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: If the same character appears more than once in the data item referenced by identifier-6 or in literal-4, the first occurrence of the character is used for replacement.

rows.subject: INTERFACE-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.6.3 OK, SR 2): 'Interface-name-2 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of this source element.' Code: each INHERITS name goes through OoNameResolution.Resolve(Want.Interface) whose scope is the REPOSITORY of the referring source element (ancestor walk, §8.4.6.4). Probes (--std 2002): probe/interface-id-paragraph/sr2_norepo.cob (N2B INHERITS FROM N2A, N2A defined but not in N2B's REPOSITORY) -> COBOLNET0840 '...not declared in the REPOSITORY paragraph of this source element... (ISO §11.6.3 SR2; ISO §8.4.6.4)'; sr2_undefined.cob (NOSUCH in REPOSITORY, never defined) -> COBOLNET0840; sr2_classname.cob (a CLASS name in REPOSITORY named in INHERITS) -> COBOLNET0840 (Want.Interface excludes classes). The §8.4.6.4 containing-definition exception lets an interface name itself, which SR3 then rejects (sr3_self). Positive: pos.cob compiles. Minor wording nit only ('no such an interface'). No existing spec-derived golden for the INHERITS arm -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO facility, introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; interface definitions are rejected COBOLNET0900 at 85)
rows.rule-text: Interface-name-2 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of this source element.

rows.subject: INTERFACE-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.6.3 OK, SR 3): 'Interface-name-2 shall not inherit directly or indirectly from interface-name-1.' Code: after resolution, a DFS from each interface over Inherits reports COBOLNET0840 'the INHERITS graph is cyclic (ISO §11.6.3 SR3)' when it reaches itself. Probes (--std 2002): probe/interface-id-paragraph/sr3_self.cob (A INHERITS A) -> 0840; sr3_cycle.cob (A->B->A) -> 0840 on both; sr3_indirect.cob (A->C->B->A, three-deep) -> 0840 on all three. Acyclic diamond-free multi-base pos.cob compiles. No existing spec-derived test -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO facility, introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; interface definitions are rejected COBOLNET0900 at 85)
rows.rule-text: Interface-name-2 shall not inherit directly or indirectly from interface-name-1.

rows.subject: INTERFACE-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.6.4 OK, GR 2): 'The INHERITS clause specifies the names of interfaces that are inherited by interface-name-1 according to 9.3.10, Interface inheritance.' §9.3.10 (--check OK): 'The inheriting interface has all the method specifications defined for the inherited interface definition or definitions, including any method specifications that the inherited definition or definitions inherited.' Code: grammar interfaceDefinition parses INHERITS FROM? interfaceName+ (repetition supported; A.4.10 item 2 claimed per PB285); OoClassTable resolves each into isym.Inherits; AllPrototypes walks the transitive closure; EmitInterfaceUnit emits the bases as C# interface bases (transitive by construction). Probe probe/interface-id-paragraph/pos.cob: IFPC3 INHERITS FROM IFPA IFPB (two bases, no own methods); class IFPC IMPLEMENTS IFPC3; SET an IFPA-typed reference TO the IFPC3 reference and INVOKE SPEAK through it, INVOKE WALK and SPEAK through the IFPC3 reference -> SPEAK / WALK / SPEAK (all inherited methods present, derived conforms to base). The 9.3.10 sentence 'shall always conform to each of the inherited interfaces' is the conformance obligation SR-11.6.3-5 owns (DIVERGES there). No existing golden isolates the multi-base inheritance surface (pb972_raising_conformance / pb451_set_format5_self_sender use single-base INHERITS for other rules) -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the OO facility, introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; interface definitions are rejected COBOLNET0900 at 85)
rows.rule-text: The INHERITS clause specifies the names of interfaces that are inherited by interface-name-1 according to 9.3.10, Interface inheritance.

rows.subject: INVOKE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If identifier-3 does not reference an address-identifier, identifier-3 is a receiving operand.' (--check OK §14.9.23.3 20)). OoBindInvocationArg resolves every non-CONTENT identifier (explicit BY REFERENCE and the GR6-assumed one) through host.Expr.ResolveReceiving (kb/Work PB881), so receiving prohibitions apply: BY REFERENCE CR (a CONSTANT RECORD) -> COBOLNET1548 citing §13.18.15.3 SR2 (probe pe3 line 2); the universal path also uses ResolveReceiving. Positive: BY REFERENCE X5 writes back (pd4). No dedicated spec-derived test. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)
rows.rule-text: If identifier-3 does not reference an address-identifier, identifier-3 is a receiving operand.

rows.subject: INVOKE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Identifier-4 is a receiving operand.' (--check OK §14.9.23.3 22)). Every RETURNING arm (resolved, NEW, SELF-NEW, universal) resolves identifier-4 through ResolveReceiving: a constant-name -> COBOLNET1548 (§13.10.4 GR1; pe2), a CONSTANT RECORD -> 1548 (§13.18.15.3 SR2; pe5); a legal receiver is written (pe6 prints 0042). Cosmetic: the resolved path adds a redundant second 0828 'not resolvable to storage' after the chokepoint's report (pe2/pe5) - the NEW/SELF-NEW arms already return BoundRejected.Reported (PB236/PB881); only OoBindResolvedInvoke line ~408 still re-reports. No dedicated test. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)

rows.subject: INVOKE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'This correspondence is positional and not by name equivalence' (cite.py --check 14.9.23.4 OK, GR3). OoBindResolvedInvoke pairs argCtxs[i] with formals[i] (m.Binding.Formals ordered PD USING list), trailing OPTIONAL formals take explicit omitted slots, arity mismatch is COBOLNET0828 (§14.8.2.1). Probe c1.cob `INVOKE OBJ "M" USING A BY CONTENT A` with formals L1 L2: L1 (by reference) write reached A (A=0077), L2 kept the content copy 0005 — each argument landed on its positional formal. No spec-derived multi-argument positional golden located -> test-ref empty. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE / OO is a COBOL-2002 introduction)
rows.rule-text: The sequence of arguments in the USING phrase of the INVOKE statement and the corresponding formal parameters in the USING phrase of the invoked method's procedure division header determines the correspondence between arguments and formal parameters. This correspondence is positional and not by name equivalence. NOTE The first argument corresponds to the first formal parameter, the second to the second, and the nth to the nth. The effect of the USING phrase on the activated runtime element is described in 14.3, Procedure division, general rules.

rows.subject: INVOKE statement (behavior when invoking a non-COBOL method)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §14.9.23.4 GR2 b) (cite.py OK §14.9.23.4 2)) leaves a non-COBOL method's INVOKE behaviour to the implementor; COBOL.NET's determination is that none can be designated. Verified by probe: p101b (REPOSITORY CLASS SB AS "System.Text.StringBuilder"; INVOKE SB "NEW") -> COBOLNET0823, exit 70; p101c (typed receiver, INVOKE U "ToString") -> COBOLNET0825, exit 70; p101a (universal receiver, method name "ToString" in a PIC X data item) -> COBOL method HI runs, then EC-OO-METHOD fatal from CobolObject.__CobolInvoke, exit 1. Row written to §7 as DOC-A.1-101 (kb/Work PB1534/PB1522 step 3). No test pins the .NET-member case specifically (OoSpineTests.Universal_UnknownMethod_EcOoMethod and InvokeUnknownMethod_0825 pin a COBOL-unknown name through the same arm), hence Pinned by —. Adjacent open edge: REPOSITORY class resolution without an external repository, kb/Work PB1086. Side finding: the COBOLNET0825 message cites §14.9.23.3 SR4d; the rule for an object-class-name receiver is SR4 b) (cite.py OK §14.9.23.3 4) b)).
rows.rule-text: INVOKE statement (behavior when invoking a non-COBOL method). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.23, INVOKE statement, General rule 2b)

rows.subject: Identifier
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR11 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 11) OK): qualified-linage-counter is defined in 8.4.2.2 (LINAGE-COUNTER [ {OF|IN} file-name ]). Grammar arm `LINAGE_COUNTER ((OF | IN) cobolWord)?`; LinageFileOf resolves the file. Probe l5.cob (--std 85): two LINAGE files, 3 and 1 WRITEs: MOVE LINAGE-COUNTER OF F1 / IN F2 -> 04 / 02 (each file's own counter). The run-time abort of this identifier in string contexts is recorded against FMT-8.4.3.1.2 (it is the operand binding, not the qualification this rule defines). Probes under out/probe/ident with the pinned cobol.exe. [code-location note: (LINAGE_COUNTER arm)] || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023

rows.subject: Initial and last-used states of data
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.6.2.3.2 OK, case 2): static data is placed in initial state 'The first time the program in which it is described is activated after the execution of an activating statement referencing a program that possesses the initial attribute and directly or indirectly contains the program.' Code: ProgramTable.CallProgram, for n.Initial, creates a fresh instance and runs CancelContained(n) (every contained program recursively through CancelNode: instance dropped, static WS reset via StaticReset=__ResetStatics, internal connectors closed); the §14.9.18 GR2 implicit CANCEL at the INITIAL program's return does the same. The reset is applied eagerly at the container's activation rather than lazily at the containee's next activation - observationally identical because a containee is reachable only inside its container's activation. Probe probe/is3/p3.cob (INITIAL P3OUT > P3MID (non-recursive, WS M VALUE 0, internal file F) > P3IN (WS I VALUE 0)): second CALL P3OUT prints 'MID M=01 OPEN FS=00' / 'IN I=01' again - the INDIRECTLY contained P3IN is reset and P3MID's connector is in no open mode (reopen 00). Golden pb154_cancel_cascade pins the DIRECT half (RECURSIVE containee A returns to 0001 on the second CALL OUTER154); the INDIRECT half is probe-verified only (a spec-derived golden for the two-level case would harden the row). || REFUTED: CONFORMS with EMPTY test-ref (behaviour verified on legal source by probe; the cited golden is not a valid witness) — The behaviour holds on legal source: re-ran probe/is3/p3.cob with the pinned cobol.exe (INITIAL P3OUT > P3MID (file F, M VALUE 0) > P3IN): the second CALL P3OUT prints MID M=01 OPEN FS=00 / IN I=01 again. I also tried to break the eager CancelContained with a live containee (R RECURSIVE > I INITIAL > Q, Q CALLs R, R re-CALLs I while Q is active, which would throw EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE). That source is illegal under 11.10.3 SR5, so the attack does not apply. The test-ref does not hold up: pb154_cancel_cascade pins the 'direct half' with INNERA154 RECURSIVE contained in OUTER154 INITIAL. 11.10.3 SR6 forbids that, so the golden's expected A=0001 comes from non-conforming source and is not spec-derived. The pinned compiler accepts that source without a diagnostic. BinderDriver.cs:412-415 checks only a unit's own INITIAL+RECURSIVE pair (COBOLNET0886), and its comment at ~427 wrongly calls an INITIAL containee of a recursive container legal. That is an under-reject defect with no kb/Work note found (grep of the pin's kb/Work for 11.10.3 SR5/SR6 found only PB899, about 0886). || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (INITIAL attribute and contained programs exist at every edition; no Annex E change)
rows.rule-text: The first time the program in which it is described is activated after the execution of an activating statement referencing a program that possesses the initial attribute and directly or indirectly contains the program.
